  473 +// parseCents converts NUMERIC(12,2) text to exact cents. No floating
  474 +// point anywhere: fractional digits beyond 2dp fail loudly (out of
  475 +// the column's scale contract).
  476 +func parseCents(s string) (int64, error) {
  477 +    neg := false
  478 +    if strings.HasPrefix(s, "-") {
  479 +        neg = true
  480 +        s = s[1:]
  481 +    }
  482 +    parts := strings.Split(s, ".")
  483 +    if len(parts) > 2 || parts[0] == "" {
  484 +        return 0, fmt.Errorf("bad amount %q", s)
  485 +    }
  486 +    for _, c := range parts[0] {
  487 +        if c < '0' || c > '9' {
  488 +            return 0, fmt.Errorf("bad amount %q", s)
  489 +        }
  490 +    }
  491 +    frac := ""
  492 +    if len(parts) == 2 {
  493 +        frac = parts[1]
  494 +        if len(frac) > 2 {
  495 +            return 0, fmt.Errorf("amount %q exceeds 2dp", s)
  496 +        }
  497 +        for _, c := range frac {
  498 +            if c < '0' || c > '9' {
  499 +                return 0, fmt.Errorf("bad amount %q", s)
  500 +            }
  501 +        }
  502 +    }
  503 +    for len(frac) < 2 {
  504 +        frac += "0"
  505 +    }
  506 +    n, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[0]+frac, 10, 64)
  507 +    if err != nil {
  508 +        return 0, fmt.Errorf("bad amount %q", s)
  509 +    }
  510 +    if neg {
  511 +        n = -n
  512 +    }
  513 +    return n, nil
  514 +}
  515 +
  516 +// jsonEqual compares a Go value against stored JSON text semantically
  517 +// (key order and number encoding do not matter; values do).
  518 +func jsonEqual(want any, gotText string) bool {
  519 +    wantRaw, err := json.Marshal(want)
  520 +    if err != nil {
  521 +        return false
  522 +    }
  523 +    var w, g any
  524 +    if err := json.Unmarshal(wantRaw, &w); err != nil {
  525 +        return false
  526 +    }
  527 +    dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(gotText))
  528 +    dec.UseNumber()
  529 +    var g2 any
  530 +    if err := dec.Decode(&g2); err != nil {
  531 +        return false
  532 +    }
  533 +    g = normalizeNumbers(g2)
  534 +    w = normalizeNumbers(w)
  535 +    return reflect.DeepEqual(w, g)
  536 +}
  537 +
  538 +// normalizeNumbers renders every JSON number by its canonical value
  539 +// form so int64-vs-float64 encoding never compares unequal.
  540 +func normalizeNumbers(v any) any {
  541 +    switch t := v.(type) {
  542 +    case map[string]any:
  543 +        out := map[string]any{}
  544 +        for k, e := range t {
  545 +            out[k] = normalizeNumbers(e)
  546 +        }
  547 +        return out
  548 +    case []any:
  549 +        for i, e := range t {
  550 +            t[i] = normalizeNumbers(e)
  551 +        }
  552 +        return t
  553 +    case json.Number:
  554 +        return t.String()
  555 +    case float64:
  556 +        return strconv.FormatFloat(t, 'f', -1, 64)
  557 +    default:
  558 +        return v
  559 +    }
  560 +}

  569 +        }

  571 +    return false
  572 +}

  574 +func mismatchDetail(a, b string) string {
  575 +    if a == b {
  576 +        return ""
  577 +    }
  578 +    return fmt.Sprintf("ledger %q want %q", trunc(a), trunc(b))
  579 +}
  580 +
  581 +func trunc(s string) string {
  582 +    if len(s) > 64 {
  583 +        return s[:64] + "…"
  584 +    }
  585 +    return s
  586 +}

    1 +// Command auditor is the independent verifier (prompt8 §5.2/§5.3). It
    2 +// holds its OWN trusted state (separate dir/volume from the writer),

  242 +// checkPin verifies the stack identity in a fresh temp dir: verify the
  243 +// anchor tx from scratch, then compare the observed server UUID and
  244 +// state hash against the pinned values. Any mismatch exits loudly
  245 +// before the main state dir is touched.
  246 +func checkPin(ctx context.Context, host string, port int, user, pass, db,
        uuid string, tx uint64, hash string) error {
  247 +    dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "audit-pin-")
  248 +    if err != nil {
  249 +        return err
  250 +    }
  251 +    defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
  252 +    app, err := ledger.DialDir(ctx, host, port, user, pass, db, dir)
  253 +    if err != nil {
  254 +        return fmt.Errorf("dial: %w", err)
  255 +    }
  256 +    defer app.Close(ctx)
  257 +    if err := app.VerifiedTx(ctx, tx); err != nil {
  258 +        return fmt.Errorf("anchor tx %d: %w", tx, err)
  259 +    }
  260 +    gotUUID, err := stateServerUUID(dir)
  261 +    if err != nil {
  262 +        return fmt.Errorf("uuid: %w", err)
  263 +    }
  264 +    if gotUUID != uuid {
  265 +        return fmt.Errorf("server UUID %q != pinned %q", gotUUID, uuid)
  266 +    }
  267 +    gotHash, err := hashStateDir(dir)
  268 +    if err != nil {
  269 +        return fmt.Errorf("hash: %w", err)
  270 +    }
  271 +    if gotHash != hash {
  272 +        return fmt.Errorf("state hash %q != pinned %q", gotHash, hash)
  273 +    }
  274 +    return nil
  275 +}
  276 +
  277 +// ceremonyAnchor captures the committable anchor: verify tx 1 (the
  278 +// immutable history root) from a fresh dir and hash the result. The
  279 +// anchor is stable for the life of the volume: tx 1 never changes,
  280 +// and the dir hash after verifying exactly tx 1 is deterministic
  281 +// (proven: two fresh dirs, identical hashes).
  282 +func ceremonyAnchor(ctx context.Context, host string, port int, user, pas
       s, db string) (anchor, error) {
  283 +    var a anchor
  284 +    a.AnchorTx = 1
  285 +    dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "audit-genesis-")
  286 +    if err != nil {
  287 +        return a, err
  288 +    }
  289 +    defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
  290 +    app, err := ledger.DialDir(ctx, host, port, user, pass, db, dir)
  291 +    if err != nil {
  292 +        return a, fmt.Errorf("dial: %w", err)
  293 +    }
  294 +    defer app.Close(ctx)
  295 +    if err := app.VerifiedTx(ctx, 1); err != nil {
  296 +        return a, fmt.Errorf("anchor tx 1: %w", err)
  297 +    }
  298 +    a.ServerUUID, err = stateServerUUID(dir)
  299 +    if err != nil {
  300 +        return a, err
  301 +    }
  302 +    a.StateHash, err = hashStateDir(dir)
  303 +    if err != nil {
  304 +        return a, err
  305 +    }
  306 +    return a, nil
  307 +}
  308 +
  309 +// stateServerUUID reads the server UUID the client pinned in its
  310 +// identity file (format: {"serverUUID": ..., "serverIdentity": ...}).
  311 +func stateServerUUID(dir string) (string, error) {
  312 +    ents, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
  313 +    if err != nil {
  314 +        return "", err
  315 +    }
  316 +    for _, e := range ents {
  317 +        if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".identity-") {
  318 +            continue
  319 +        }
  320 +        raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
  321 +        if err != nil {
  322 +            return "", err
  323 +        }
  324 +        var v struct {
  325 +            ServerUUID string `json:"serverUUID"`
  326 +        }
  327 +        if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &v); err != nil {
  328 +            return "", fmt.Errorf("identity file: %w", err)
  329 +        }
  330 +        if v.ServerUUID == "" {
  331 +            return "", fmt.Errorf("identity file has no serverUUID")
  332 +        }
  333 +        return v.ServerUUID, nil
  334 +    }
  335 +    return "", fmt.Errorf("no identity file in %s", dir)
  336 +}
  337 +
  338 +func resolveTxIDs(list string) ([]uint64, error) {
  339 +    var out []uint64
  340 +    for _, s := range strings.Split(list, ",") {
  341 +        n, err := strconv.ParseUint(strings.TrimSpace(s), 10, 64)
  342 +        if err != nil {
  343 +            return nil, fmt.Errorf("bad tx id %q", s)
  344 +        }
  345 +        out = append(out, n)
  346 +    }
  347 +    if len(out) == 0 {
  348 +        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no tx ids: pass --txs")
  349 +    }
  350 +    return out, nil
  351 +}
  352 +
  353 +func dirIsEmpty(dir string) (bool, error) {
  354 +    if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
  355 +        return false, err
  356 +    }
  357 +    ents, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
  358 +    if err != nil {
  359 +        return false, err
  360 +    }
  361 +    return len(ents) == 0, nil
  362 +}
  363 +
  364 +// hashStateDir hashes (relative path, bytes) over the state dir. Paths
  365 +// must be relative: absolute paths would make the hash dir-dependent
  366 +// and no committed anchor could ever match (found by probe).
  367 +func hashStateDir(dir string) (string, error) {
  368 +    var files []string
  369 +    if err := filepath.Walk(dir, func(p string, info os.FileInfo, err err
       or) error {
  370 +        if err != nil || info.IsDir() {
  371 +            return err
  372 +        }
  373 +        rel, err := filepath.Rel(dir, p)
  374 +        if err != nil {
  375 +            return err
  376 +        }
  377 +        files = append(files, rel)
  378 +        return nil
  379 +    }); err != nil {
  380 +        return "", err
  381 +    }
  382 +    sort.Strings(files)
  383 +    h := sha256.New()
  384 +    for _, f := range files {
  385 +        raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, f))
  386 +        if err != nil {
  387 +            return "", err
  388 +        }
  389 +        h.Write([]byte(f))
  390 +        h.Write(raw)
  391 +    }
  392 +    return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)), nil
  393 +}

  395 +func postWebhook(url string, body []byte) {
  396 +    req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewReader(body))
  397 +    if err != nil {
  398 +        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "auditor: webhook build:", err)
  399 +        return
  400 +    }
  401 +    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  402 +    resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  403 +    if err != nil {
  404 +        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "auditor: webhook post:", err)
  405 +        return
  406 +    }
  407 +    defer resp.Body.Close()
  408 +    fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "auditor: webhook status %s\n", resp.Status)
  409 +}

  415 +        return h, 3322
  416 +    }
  417 +    return h, port
  418 +}

   34 +// buildAuditor compiles the auditor binary into a temp dir.
   35 +func buildAuditor(t *testing.T) string {
   36 +    t.Helper()
   37 +    bin := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "auditor")
   38 +    cmd := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", bin, "./cmd/auditor")
   39 +    cmd.Dir = ".."
   40 +    if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   41 +        t.Fatalf("build auditor: %v\n%s", err, out)
   42 +    }
   43 +    return bin
   44 +}

   46 +// runAuditor executes the auditor, failing loudly; returns stdout.
   47 +func runAuditor(t *testing.T, bin string, args ...string) string {
   48 +    t.Helper()
   49 +    code, stdout, stderr := runAuditorCode(t, bin, args...)
   50 +    if code != 0 {
   51 +        t.Fatalf("auditor %v: exit %d\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", args, c
       ode, stdout, stderr)
   52 +    }
   53 +    return stdout

   56 +// runAuditorCode executes the auditor with split streams (the JSON
   57 +// report stays parseable: stderr carries the genesis line).
   58 +func runAuditorCode(t *testing.T, bin string, args ...string) (int, strin
       g, string) {
   59 +    t.Helper()
   60 +    cmd := exec.Command(bin, args...)
   61 +    var stdout, stderr strings.Builder
   62 +    cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
   63 +    err := cmd.Run()
   64 +    if err == nil {
   65 +        return 0, stdout.String(), stderr.String()
   66 +    }
   67 +    if ee, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
   68 +        return ee.ExitCode(), stdout.String(), stderr.String()
   69 +    }
   70 +    t.Fatalf("auditor %v: %v", args, err)
   71 +    return -1, "", ""
   72 +}

  128 +// finalizeBatteryMonth runs a full month on the recycled battery
  129 +// employer and convergently approves it; returns the validated run.
  130 +func finalizeBatteryMonth(t *testing.T, pool *pgxpool.Pool, bin string, a
       pprover string) string {
  131 +    t.Helper()
  132 +    ctx := context.Background()
  133 +    benv := map[string]string{"POC_EMPLOYER": authEmployer, "POC_PERIOD":
        authPeriod}
  134 +    cmd := exec.Command(bin, "--approval-timeout", "150s")
  135 +    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
  136 +    for k, v := range benv {
  137 +        cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, k+"="+v)
  138 +    }
  139 +    if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
  140 +        t.Fatal(err)
  141 +    }
  142 +    done := make(chan error, 1)
  143 +    go func() { done <- cmd.Wait() }()
  144 +    var runID string
  145 +    waitFor(t, "battery month persisted", 120*time.Second, func() bool {
  146 +        return pool.QueryRow(ctx,
  147 +            `SELECT r.id FROM payroll_run r JOIN employer e ON e.id = r.e
       mployer_id
  148 +              JOIN poc_run_output o ON o.run_id = r.id
  149 +              WHERE e.code = $1`, authEmployer).Scan(&runID) == nil
  150 +    })
  151 +    deadline := time.Now().Add(240 * time.Second)
  152 +    approved := false
  153 +    for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
  154 +        approveOut, approveErr := runBin(t, bin, benv, "approve", "--run-
       id", runID,
  155 +            "--decision", "approve", "--approver", approver)
  156 +        if approveErr == nil {
  157 +            approved = true
  158 +        } else if !strings.Contains(approveOut, "no rows in result set")
       {
  159 +            t.Fatalf("approve: %v\n%s", approveErr, approveOut)
  160 +        }
  161 +        select {
  162 +        case err := <-done:
  163 +            if err != nil {
  164 +                t.Fatalf("battery month: %v", err)
  165 +            }
  166 +            goto completed
  167 +        case <-time.After(20 * time.Second):
  168 +        }
  169 +    }
  170 +    _ = cmd.Process.Kill()
  171 +    t.Fatal("battery month did not complete after approval")
  172 +completed:
  173 +    if !approved {
  174 +        t.Fatal("approve never succeeded")
  175 +    }
  176 +    return runID
  177 +}

  304 +// checkFailed reports whether the named check failed anywhere.
  305 +func checkFailed(rep auditReport, name string) bool {
  306 +    for _, g := range rep.Global {
  307 +        if g.Name == name && !g.Pass {
  308 +            return true
  309 +        }
  310 +    }
  311 +    for _, e := range rep.Events {
  312 +        for _, c := range e.Checks {
  313 +            if c.Name == name && !c.Pass {
  314 +                return true
  315 +            }
  316 +        }
  317 +    }
  318 +    return false
  319 +}

  439 +// TestGenesis_PinEnforced proves §5.3: the committed anchor pins the
  440 +// live stack (canary), wrong pins exit 2 before any trust decision,
  441 +// and a tampered auditor state dir fails verification.
  442 +func TestGenesis_PinEnforced(t *testing.T) {
  443 +    auditEnv(t)
  444 +    auditor := buildAuditor(t)
  445 +    raw, err := os.ReadFile("../gate/immudb-genesis.json")
  446 +    if err != nil {
  447 +        t.Fatalf("committed anchor: %v", err)
  448 +    }
  449 +    var anch struct {

  451 +        Tx     uint64 `json:"anchor_tx"`
  452 +        TxHash string `json:"tx_hash"`
  453 +    }
  454 +    if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &anch); err != nil {
  455 +        t.Fatalf("parse anchor: %v", err)
  456 +    }
  457 +    pinArgs := []string{"--expect-uuid", anch.UUID, "--expect-tx", fmt.Sp
       rint(anch.Tx),
  458 +        "--expect-tx-hash", anch.TxHash}

  460 +    if code, stdout, _ := runAuditorCode(t, auditor, append([]string{
  461 +        "--state-dir", t.TempDir(), "--accept-genesis", "--txs", "1",
  462 +    }, pinArgs...)...); code != 0 || !strings.Contains(stdout, `"overall"
       : "pass"`) {
  463 +        t.Fatalf("anchor canary failed (stack recreated? re-run the genes
       is ceremony): exit=%d\n%s", code, stdout)
  464 +    }
  465 +    // Wrong pins exit 2 (usage/trust failure, never a pass).
  466 +    for _, bad := range [][]string{
  467 +        {"--expect-uuid", "WRONG", "--expect-tx", fmt.Sprint(anch.Tx), "-
       -expect-tx-hash", anch.TxHash},
  468 +        {"--expect-uuid", anch.UUID, "--expect-tx", fmt.Sprint(anch.Tx),
       "--expect-tx-hash", strings.Repeat("0", 64)},
  469 +        {"--expect-uuid", anch.UUID},
  470 +    } {
  471 +        args := append([]string{"--state-dir", t.TempDir(), "--accept-gen
       esis", "--txs", "1"}, bad...)
  472 +        if code, _, _ := runAuditorCode(t, auditor, args...); code != 2 {
  473 +            t.Fatalf("bad pin %v: exit=%d, want 2", bad, code)
  474 +        }
  475 +    }
  476 +    // Tampered state dir: verify once, flip a byte, re-verify fails.
  477 +    dir := t.TempDir()
  478 +    if code, _, _ := runAuditorCode(t, auditor,
  479 +        "--state-dir", dir, "--accept-genesis", "--txs", "1"); code != 0
       {
  480 +        t.Fatalf("baseline liveness exit=%d", code)
  481 +    }
  482 +    ents, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
  483 +    if err != nil {
  484 +        t.Fatal(err)
  485 +    }
  486 +    flipped := false
  487 +    for _, e := range ents {
  488 +        if strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".state-") {

  490 +            raw, err := os.ReadFile(p)
  491 +            if err != nil || len(raw) == 0 {
  492 +                t.Fatal(err)
  493 +            }
  494 +            raw[len(raw)-1] ^= 0xff
  495 +            if err := os.WriteFile(p, raw, 0o600); err != nil {
  496 +                t.Fatal(err)
  497 +            }
  498 +            flipped = true
  499 +        }
  500 +    }
  501 +    if !flipped {
  502 +        t.Fatal("no state file to tamper")
  503 +    }

       s", "1"); code == 0 {

  506 +    }

   41 +## 1. Original root causes
   42 +
   43 +### PG-1 — Application-side fabrication path (adversarial review §PG)
   44 +The app role held direct INSERT/UPDATE on payroll tables, so a
   45 +compromised or buggy application could fabricate a snapshot and mark
   46 +it valid without ever passing the capture gate. Reproduced live in
   47 +Phase A (Gate B): app-role INSERT into `payroll_snapshot` succeeded.
   48 +Root mechanism: authority lived in application code, not in the
   49 +database; direct SQL could bypass every check.
   50 +
   51 +### DB-3 — Capture identity accepted stale results (adversarial review §D
       B)
   52 +Month reruns did not re-execute: the same capture ID discarded new
   53 +input, so a rerun silently returned the previous outcome instead of
   54 +the current truth. Reproduced live in Phase A. Root mechanism:
   55 +idempotency keyed on the attempt rather than bound to (business run,
   56 +input digest).
   57 +
   58 +### IM-7 — Auditor verified existence, never content (review §IM)
   59 +The auditor called `VerifiedTxByID` per tx and reported pass — it
   60 +never compared ledger bytes against PostgreSQL content. A swapped or
   61 +mutated record verified clean. Reproduced live in Phase A (swapped
   62 +and mutated records audited PASS). Root mechanism: no content
   63 +binding anywhere in the verify path; the backlinks file was trusted
   64 +input rather than a claim to check.
   65 +
   66 +### Contributing causes
   67 +- IM-9: recovery read the idempotency marker with unverified `Get`
   68 +  (single unverified read on the link path).
   69 +- IM-10: retry accounting could mark an appended-but-unlinked row
   70 +  failed, orphaning attested evidence by threshold.
   71 +- IM-11: backlink PK `(pg_table, pg_id)` blocked legitimate
   72 +  correction events for the same artifact.
   73 +- IM-12/IM-13: outbox/backlink writes were direct app SQL; no
   74 +  production path enqueued real evidence.
   75 +- DB-4/DB-5: no proven crash-retry story; returned results were
   76 +  trusted without persisted-state corroboration.
   77 +- IM-1/IM-2/IM-3: genesis never pinned or compared; writer and
   78 +  auditor shared the superuser; no auditor read-only identity.
   79 +- IM-8: no host-corruption evidence (server-side file tamper).
   80 +
   81 +## 2. Corrected architecture
   82 +
   83 +PostgreSQL authorizes; DBOS durably executes; Go calculates from
   84 +captured records; PostgreSQL persists results; immudb anchors
   85 +evidence; the auditor independently reconstructs and verifies.
   86 +
   87 +- Capture/validate/approve/close/enqueue are `SECURITY DEFINER`
   88 +  functions owned by `migration_admin`, with `search_path =
   89 +  pg_catalog`, explicit `EXECUTE` grants, and trigger guards. The app
   90 +  role has SELECT plus narrow EXECUTE — every direct fabrication
   91 +  write fails 42501 (proven, not asserted).
   92 +- The DBOS month workflow (Stages A–G) runs capture inside the
   93 +  transactional boundary, calculates from reloaded snapshot rows,
   94 +  persists lines/payslips, waits for approval, validates, and
   95 +  enqueues. Attempt identity is unique + Reject-on-reuse; business
   96 +  identity is (employer, period, kind) + input digest, with
   97 +  adopt-or-conflict convergence (`poc_run_consistency`).
   98 +- The outbox worker appends canonical evidence records under
   99 +  MustNotExist preconditions, recovers through VERIFIED reads only,
  100 +  and links via the squat-proof recorder. Proven appends can never
  101 +  be discarded (trigger-enforced, even against the owner).
  102 +- The auditor is a separate identity (read-only immudb user +
  103 +  SELECT-only PG role, own state dir, pinned genesis) that rebuilds
  104 +  expected evidence from PG sources, re-executes the payroll, and
  105 +  compares everything against verified ledger bytes.
  106 +

  275 +## 10. Remaining limitations (honest, none failing §11)
  276 +
  277 +1. Calculator-version binding, not implementation provenance:
  278 +   `calc_digest = sha256(version label)`. A compromised calculator
  279 +   binary is outside the stated threat model (noted in code).
  280 +2. `PackDigest` = first pin's digest; multi-pin joint digest is
  281 +   future work (single-pin fixture; documented in code).
  282 +3. Period `"2026-10"` hardcoded in Stage C and auditor alike
  283 +   (shared constant形状 — same value both sides; fixture-scoped).
  284 +4. Auditor `SHA256` check hashes `payload::text` as the instance
  285 +   serializes it (same-instance determinism; cross-version jsonb
  286 +   text form not staked).
  287 +5. `supersedes` predecessor lookup has no sub-microsecond tiebreak
  288 +   (matches enqueue exactly; ties unobserved).
  289 +6. Production ledger hardening (TLS, signing keys, stable volumes,
  290 +   retention, monitoring) is a promotion checklist
  291 +   (`P8-PROD-MIGRATION-PROPOSAL.md`), NOT implemented in the POC.
  292 +7. immudb BSL-1.1 counsel review still pending (~2030-09-02 note).
  293 +8. Conventional-job baseline still unmeasured (classified
  294 +   NOT RUN throughout; never claimed).
  295 +9. DBOS `Shutdown` pool leak persists upstream (ClosePoolTimeout
  296 +   workaround retained + documented).
  297 +10. Clock/attendance/terms/leave/comp writers remain gate-only
  298 +    (no period mapping) — recorded proposal limitation.
  299 +11. IM-8 mechanism observed is server-side envelope detection;
  300 +    proof-vs-forged-bytes is covered compositionally (state-tamper
  301 +    + pin + binding checks), not by a forged-serving server cell.
  302 +12. Stale `poc_ledger_backlink` rows accumulate (append-only by
  303 +    design); audit_event retention hygiene still open.
